title: The first House set up for people was at Bakkah.
subtitle: Where worship on earth began
then: Ibn Kathir explains the Ka'bah was built by Ibrahim, whose religion others claimed. The Prophet ﷺ was asked which mosque came first and said {idea}al-Masjid al-Haram, then al-Aqsa, forty years later{/idea}. He added: {reward}wherever prayer time finds you, pray, for the whole earth is a mosque{/reward}.
now: You may never have seen the Ka'bah except on a screen, yet you turn toward it five times a day from a bedroom, an office, a parking lot. {idea}The first House is the center of your direction.{/idea}
old: Makkah is far away, something for one trip in my life.
new: I face the first House every day. The blessing it holds reaches me through every prayer.
try: At your next prayer, pause before takbir and picture the House you are facing.

title: Clear signs, safety, and a journey owed to Allah.
subtitle: The House that invites whoever can reach it
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the Maqam is the stone Ibrahim stood on to raise the walls while {idea}Isma'il handed him the stones{/idea}, and Mujahid said his footprints remain on it. Even before Islam, a man in fear {reward}was safe inside the Haram{/reward}.
now: You have a savings jar labeled "Hajj someday" that keeps getting borrowed from. Or you have already been and the memory is fading. {idea}The invitation stands.{/idea} {reward}Allah needs nothing from it. You do.{/reward}
old: Hajj is a duty for later, when life is settled.
new: The House is an invitation to safety and nearness, meant for me while I am able.
try: If you have not been, write down one real step toward Hajj. If you have, make dua for someone who longs to go.

title: Why reject the signs while Allah is Witness?
subtitle: Knowing, refusing, and being seen
then: Ibn Kathir notes that earlier prophets had {reward}brought good news of the coming Prophet ﷺ{/reward}. Those who knew this still {trap}rejected him{/trap}. Allah reminds them that He witnesses all they do.
now: You read the verse, you know it applies to you, and you scroll past. No one in the room noticed. {idea}Someone did.{/idea}
old: If no one sees me ignore what I know, it doesn't matter.
new: Allah witnesses what I do with what I know, even in a quiet room.
try: Act on one thing you already know you should do, today, simply because He sees.

title: Why block others from the path and make it look crooked?
subtitle: Turning people away from good

row.title: "it's crooked"
sub: while they knew it was straight

then: The verse continues the address: why {trap}turn the believers away from Allah's path{/trap}, trying to make it seem crooked, while you are witnesses? Ibn Kathir says they {idea}knew what the Messenger ﷺ brought was the truth{/idea}.
now: Your friend starts praying again and you joke, "Here comes the sheikh." Your sibling wears hijab for the first time and you ask if she is sure. {trap}A small laugh can push someone off a path.{/trap} {idea}Be the one who makes it easier.{/idea}
old: I'm only joking. It's their choice anyway.
new: My words can make the straight path look crooked to someone. I want them to make it look beautiful.
try: Encourage one person today who is trying to come closer to Allah.

title: Obey the wrong voices and they will turn you back.
subtitle: Who you take direction from
then: The believers are warned that obeying a party who {trap}envy them for the favor Allah gave{/trap} would lead them back to disbelief. Ibn Kathir links it to another verse about those who wished the believers would turn away {idea}out of their own envy{/idea}.
now: The influencer you watch daily slowly shapes what you think is normal, what is cringe, what is old-fashioned. You never decided to follow him. {trap}You just kept obeying the feed.{/trap} {idea}Notice who is steering.{/idea}
old: What I watch and listen to doesn't change what I believe.
new: Whoever I keep obeying, even passively, slowly becomes my guide.
try: Look at the three accounts you watch most. Ask honestly where each is steering you.

title: How could you disbelieve with the verses right here?
subtitle: Holding firmly to Allah

row.title: those after
sub: who found only pages and believed

then: Ibn Kathir cites a hadith: the Prophet ﷺ asked whose faith is most amazing. Not the angels, not the prophets, not the Companions, he said, but {reward}people after you who find only written pages and believe in them{/reward}. And {idea}whoever holds firmly to Allah is guided{/idea}.
now: You never saw the Prophet ﷺ. You have a mushaf on a shelf and an app on your phone. {reward}That is the faith he called amazing.{/reward} The verses are still here, recited to you.
old: Faith was easier for people who lived with the Prophet ﷺ.
new: Believing through the pages alone is the faith the Prophet ﷺ admired, and the verses are still with me.
try: Open the Quran today and read one page slowly, as if it were being recited to you.

title: Fear Allah as He deserves, and die only in submission.
subtitle: Living the way you hope to end

row.title: a last-minute fix
sub: I'll sort it at the end

then: Ibn Mas'ud explained taqwa as Allah's due: {idea}obeyed and not defied, remembered and not forgotten, thanked and not unthanked{/idea}. Ibn Kathir adds that a person dies upon how they lived. Three nights before he died, the Prophet ﷺ said {reward}die only thinking well of Allah{/reward}.
now: Monday morning, inbox open, you forgot Allah until lunch. Payday, you forgot to say alhamdulillah. {idea}Taqwa is remembering in those exact moments.{/idea} {reward}And through it all, think well of Him.{/reward}
old: As long as I'm right with Allah at the end, I'm fine.
new: I end the way I live, so I keep Him remembered and thanked now, and think well of Him.
try: Set three moments today, waking, lunch, bed, to remember and thank Allah in one sentence.

title: Hold Allah's rope together. He turned enemies into brothers.
subtitle: Unity as a gift to remember
then: Ibn Kathir says this came about the Aws and Khazraj of Madinah, who had {trap}fought long wars with great hatred{/trap}. Islam made them {reward}brothers who loved each other{/reward}. At Hunayn the Prophet ﷺ reminded them: were you not divided, and Allah united you?
now: The cousins who haven't spoken since the wedding. The mosque committee split over the parking lot. {trap}Old wounds kept open.{/trap} {idea}Remember who joined you in the first place.{/idea}
old: Some divisions are too deep to heal. It's just how families are.
new: Allah has joined hearts that hated each other for generations. Holding His rope together is the way.
try: Send one warm message today to someone you have drifted from or quarrelled with.

title: Let there be people who call to good and stop wrong.
subtitle: Doing your part in changing what's wrong
then: Ibn Kathir explains a group should take this task, yet it is {idea}on every member, each by ability{/idea}. He cites the Prophet ﷺ: whoever sees a wrong, change it {reward}with the hand, then the tongue, then the heart{/reward}.
now: In the office group chat someone shares a cruel joke about a coworker. Everyone sends a laughing emoji. You could stay silent, or type "not cool." {idea}Start where your ability reaches.{/idea}
old: Calling to good is the scholars' job, not mine.
new: Everyone has a share in this, starting with whatever my hand, tongue or heart can do.
try: Next time something wrong happens in front of you, do the smallest kind thing that pushes back.

title: Don't split apart after the clear proofs arrive.
subtitle: Division that follows clarity
then: Ibn Kathir says the believers are forbidden from {trap}imitating the division and discord of earlier nations{/trap}, who also abandoned enjoining good. Mu'awiyah, on Hajj, warned that if they did not {idea}hold to what came from their Prophet ﷺ{/idea}, others would hold to it even less.
now: The argument at the mosque about which way to do something minor turns into two groups that stop greeting each other. {trap}Same Book, same Prophet ﷺ, two camps.{/trap} {idea}Disagree without splitting.{/idea}
old: If I'm right on this point, it's fine to break off from those who aren't.
new: Splitting after clear guidance is the warning itself. Unity is part of following the proof.
try: Greet warmly today someone you disagree with on a religious point.

title: On that Day, some faces brighten and some darken.
subtitle: What shows on your face at the end
then: Ibn Abbas said bright faces belong to {reward}those of the Sunnah and the community{/reward}, dark ones to those of innovation and division. Al-Hasan said the dark-faced who are asked {trap}did you disbelieve after your belief{/trap} are the hypocrites.
now: You catch your face in a dark phone screen after an hour of gossip. Or you see it glow at the end of a long night prayer. {idea}Faces carry what you did.{/idea}
old: What I do privately doesn't show on me.
new: On that Day my deeds will show on my face. I want it to carry light.
try: Do one quiet good deed today that no one will see, hoping it brightens your face that Day.

title: Bright faces live inside Allah's mercy, forever.
subtitle: The end the verses are pointing you toward
then: After the warning, the verse turns to {reward}those whose faces will be bright{/reward}. Ibn Kathir explains they are in Allah's mercy, Paradise, {idea}where they will never desire to be moved{/idea}.
now: You come home after a long trip, drop your bag, and feel that sigh: home. Now imagine a home you never want to leave, and the verse calls it {reward}mercy{/reward}.
old: Paradise is a reward I have to fully earn on my own.
new: Paradise is called Allah's mercy. I work for it and I hope in it.
try: Ask Allah for His mercy and Paradise today, by name, after one of your prayers.

title: These verses are recited in truth. Allah wants no injustice.
subtitle: The warnings come from a just Lord

row.title: truth
sub: the real picture of both worlds

row.title: to be harsh
sub: to scare for its own sake

then: After describing bright and dark faces, Allah says these verses are recited {reward}in truth{/reward}. Ibn Kathir explains He is the Just Ruler who {idea}never treats His creatures with injustice{/idea}, needing nothing from anyone.
now: A doctor who tells you the hard truth about your blood test is not being cruel. She wants you well. {idea}The warnings you just read are like that.{/idea}
old: Warnings about the Day make Allah sound harsh.
new: The warnings come from a Lord who wants no injustice for me. They are the truth told in time.
try: Reread one warning verse today and ask what it is protecting you from.
